answer: Identity Validation via Costly Stakes This mechanism requires each agent to deposit a collateral in a common fund, creating a financial bridge against dishonest behaviors. To signal their authenticity, agents must renew their stakes periodically. An attacker cloning identities faces the immense cost of multiple stakes, as each clone demands its own deposit. If an agent is found to be operating multiple identities, their deposits are forfeited. The cost per identity thus becomes prohibitively high, resulting in fewer dishonest actors.
